title: LocAgent: Graph-Guided LLM Agents for Code Localization

model.params_source: assumed (the paper states no decoding parameters for the baseline scaffolds; it only names the snapshot, 'GPT-4o (GPT-4o-2024-0513)', in the Table 4 caption)

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: the standard 300-instance SWE-bench Lite test split (Sec. 5.1)
task.approximation: SWE-agent is a multi-turn agent with a shell and file-editing tools inside a per-instance repository checkout; a run is tens of tool-calling turns per instance, not a single chat completion, so the runner cannot execute it

items.source: huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Lite (also mirrored as SWE-bench/SWE-bench_Lite); LocAgent's own code is at github.com/gersteinlab/LocAgent (reachable 2026-09-19, HTTP 200)

fields.label: the files touched by the gold patch

items.license: unknown (the princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Lite dataset card carries no licence tag)
items.note: the localisation target is derived from the gold patch, so the label is a post-processing step over the dataset rather than a column
items.checks: the hf parquet listing resolves and the test split loads (300 rows, 3.5 MB, columns repo / instance_id / base_commit / patch / test_patch / problem_statement / hints_text / created_at / version / FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS / environment_setup_commit); --prepare then stops in render because no prompt is printed for this cell

prompt.source_location: Sec. 5.3 / Appendix C.1 (implementation details of the baselines). Appendix A.3 prints only LOCAGENT's own prompt (Figure 8); the four baseline scaffolds - Agentless, SWE-agent, MoatlessTools, OpenHands - are run with their published prompts, which this paper does not reprint.
prompt.verbatim: none (the SWE-agent prompt behind the 57.30 cell is not in the paper)

output.postprocess: the localisation is read from the agent's trajectory (the files it opened/edited), then ranked
output.parse_paper: unstated in this paper; it follows the SWE-agent scaffold's own output handling

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: file-level Acc@1: share of the 300 instances for which the single top-ranked file predicted by the agent is one of the files that must be changed (Sec. 5.2)
metric.original_location: Table 4, block Agent-Based / SWE-agent, row GPT-4o, column File(%) Acc@1

open_points: prompt not printed: the cell is produced by the third-party SWE-agent scaffold as the LocAgent authors configured it; neither the scaffold prompts nor their configuration are reprinted, so a reproduction would be a re-implementation rather than a re-run of the published prompt.

sandbox: SWE-agent needs a per-instance repository checkout and a container with shell and editor tools, and a run costs tens of model turns per instance. That infrastructure is outside the Tier B runner and is a separate engineering decision.

label: file-level accuracy is scored against the files touched by the gold patch, which has to be derived from the SWE-bench Lite patch column; the ranking that turns an agent trajectory into Acc@1/3/5 is not specified in the paper.
notes: The three other agent scaffolds in Table 4 (Agentless, MoatlessTools, OpenHands) have the same GPT-4o rows and the same blockers. LocAgent's own model is a fine-tuned Qwen2.5, i.e. not a live-listed OpenAI snapshot.
